pinned-time-after-the-captured-horizon.text: Pinned time after the captured horizon.

As an operator writing after a time recording's former horizon, I want conversions to continue with the pinned final era's slot length and epoch size. If the provider reports another protocol major, the command must refuse by name before building. A time before the pinned system start must also refuse, while the exact start remains slot zero.

The epic's 2026-10-05 NOTE030 ruling, consumed through the commit owner's A005 and NOTE020, explicitly amends the former finite-horizon policy. NOTE022 requires a reached pre-start clamp regression and restored exact-start control. The old policy and its receipts remain history: the former interpreter refused past its finite end, and times before genesis were clamped to zero. Those observations do not establish the amended behavior. Q005's proposal to cap validity bounds at the horizon was dropped and was never implemented.

implementation-mapping.text: NetworkTime.validateNetworkTime checks the same raw genesis/history identities, network, system start, era extent and recorded horizon. It opens only the final era's eraEnd in the interpreter summary; the captured CBOR is retained and the final era's slot length, epoch size and other parameters are preserved. Floor, ceiling, slot-start and the evaluator's epoch information share that interpreter. TimeBeforeHistory refuses times earlier than the pinned start.

Each time manifest pins protocolMajor. The reviewed preprod pin is checked against its recorded evaluation parameter CBOR; the devnet recording pin is checked against its recorded parameter CBOR. Private publications derive the pin from parameters queried in the same LSQ acquisition as raw history/start/point and retain the raw parameter CBOR. A generic session remains Unbound; this private source provenance does not turn shared HTTP reads into an atomic snapshot claim.

SessionIO.parameters calls the common SessionServices.parameters guard before any builder uses parameters to construct a body. The raw provider parameters and pinned context are consumed within that build's session; a different major yields EraBeyondPinned expected actual. The terminal startup validates that guard in its own logged acquisition, and the common evaluator also checks its actual raw parameters. The retained private raw-node composition checks the major while constructing its acquired view. These are implementation entry points, not a new provider compatibility surface.

The guard has a protocolMajorGuard phase and consumes real parameter/time facts through the existing receipt observer. Later confirmation acquisitions stay separate from a prepared body's facts. Time conversion alone operates on the pinned context; the pre-build guard is a separate raw-parameter comparison.

The later 2026-10-05 NOTE031/A020 ruling explicitly adds a moving ledger translation horizon, separate from the captured artifact's former end. From the build session's observed tip and its authenticated genesis security parameter k, active-slot coefficient f and epoch length, NetworkTime.ledgerHorizon computes the first epoch boundary at or after tip + ceil(3k/f). The pinned history supplies the epoch anchor and the genesis epoch length must agree with the final era. Unbounded integer arithmetic precedes checked slot conversion. capValidityUpper selects min(existing upper, horizon - 1).

NOTE026/A021 first corrected finite-bound equality to capped upper <= lower. The later NOTE028/A022 ruling explicitly strengthens both interval shapes to a usable-after-observed-tip check: refuse when capped upper <= max(actual finite lower, observed tip + 1), with an omitted body lower imposing no constraint. Integer arithmetic prevents a wrapped tip + 1. This is caller policy, not a claim that an upper-only interval such as [0,868) is mathematically empty.

WindowPastLedgerHorizon preserves tip, horizon and the original optional lower/upper window and refuses before signing. Fold and connected fold supply Nothing for their actual omitted lower; reject and retraction retain their finite lower. No lower is added to an upper-only body. All four paths select before body construction/evaluation, through common local services; phase logging records the actual optional lower separately from the effective lower, plus tip, horizon, original upper and resulting bound. The session remains Unbound; later reads do not make this observation a snapshot promise.

The earlier moving-horizon amendment changed no validity-window size, candidate fallback list, refund, authorization, signing, state/root or token rule. The later A024 minimum and conditional harness timing amendments are stated below. The moving-horizon selection is the explicit amendment to the earlier no-capping disposition; the captured artifact end stays irrelevant to conversion. Confirmation uses the resulting capped upper slot's POSIX start plus uncapped 120 seconds, or now plus uncapped 300 seconds without an upper bound, exact-output visibility, latest-block expiry and existing recovery. The later minimum-window amendment below authorizes one bounded pre-signing horizon wait; it authorizes no repeated wait or submission retry. Genesis/epoch/node settings remain unchanged. Opening a conversion era does not open transaction validity intervals.

minimum-usable-interval.text: As a caller building under load, I require ten seconds of usable slots before signing. Parent NOTE032/A024 and slice contract v8 (2026-10-06) explicitly amend the earlier no-wait rule. The raw pinned slot conversion computes M100 on the 0.1-second devnet and M10 on one-second preprod. Empty intervals keep WindowPastLedgerHorizon; nonempty registry-limited short intervals refuse WindowTooShort without waiting. The original optional body lower is preserved.

A window made short only by the ledger horizon may wait once through the same Unbound session until ledgerHorizon(newTip) exceeds its original horizon, then construct/evaluate from the new selection. The at-or-after ceiling remains: devnet970 still yields1000;971 yields1500. Both the M-slot bound and20-second wall-clock bound apply. HorizonWaitTimedOut carries the last observed tip and horizon and occurs before signing/submission. Phase logs retain the wait and new selected tip; fresh observations do not imply a snapshot. Pure local services compute the decision without hidden clock or external effects; IO consumers perform the explicitly ruled wait.

Conditional CI timing authority applies only after an actual journey stops on WindowTooShort: increase its CI registry process/retract windows to90s/30s, retain the original profile/trigger/source receipts and measured build durations. No such change has been made merely from the ruling. Minimum10s stays fixed. The previous full-native69/3/39pending and focused1/0 receipts remain historical; a restored full native E2E with no expired-submit failures is required.

bound-model-and-limits.text: Behavioral authority remains Lean commit 872c0ecf3c7cf1a10293793523c8521d5ef9aae9. The current Model, Statements and Driver Git blobs are respectively b548e3e93af7529a968e8cd1b46996d3157baf8b, dbc07cc222e121a9ba9d344c05c53d807b657da9 and fdabc45363b2ec1d693410598cd9cda24d2bcc51; they are unchanged.

lean/Singular/Model.lean defines RetractWitness at line 1163, inPhase2 at line 1184, retractAdmission at line 1193 and exitAdmission at line 1201. Retraction requires the finite POSIX validity interval inside its request's phase two. Fold/reject admission ignores that witness. None of these definitions models HTTP, slot-to-time arithmetic, a captured history horizon or protocol-major pinning. The amended conversion/API policy is an explicitly ruled imported computation; these interval premises are not a proof of it. Concrete ledger/consensus/raw-source correctness remains a reliance boundary, and the existing early-reject correspondence hold remains visible.

verification-appendix.text: Regression controls exercise a conversion ten million slots beyond the recorded devnet horizon; the real boot builder with changed raw protocol major and zero wallet-output reads; and the former pre-start clamp at system start minus one, with exact-start floor/ceiling/slot-start accepting controls. Recorded valid slot/era boundary answers remain independently checked; recorded past-horizon refusals are retained as historical inputs with explicitly amended expectations. Existing boot accepting/refusing controls, finite retraction bounds and confirmation deadlines remain required.

Runtime source/native/argv/log receipts belong to the existing 002/003 campaign. A source-bound native component pass is not Nix packaging, an unchanged hosted-job carrier, exact-head hosted CI, full-row acceptance or a causal diagnosis of #409. The repair PR may say Fixes #409 only when hosted Demo1 is green on its exact head. All twenty public requirement rows continue to publish their uncovered dimensions; this review note promotes none.

An actual native update-terminal run exposed a separate external limit: local conversion, major-10 guard and evaluation succeeded, but the independent node returned TimeTranslationPastHorizon for upper slot 1113 against its own finite era end 1000 at observed tip 868. That failed receipt remains historical. Q006's policy hold is released only by the explicit moving-horizon ruling above; actual node restoration and unchanged hosted journeys remain required evidence. The local extension alone does not establish that an external node will translate every resulting validity bound.

The reached public reject-builder regression at tip 868 produced exclusive upper 2068 where the moving-horizon ruling requires at most 999. Recorded devnet controls check the tip-868 horizon and its exact epoch-ceiling boundaries, a wholly past-horizon window and finite-lower equality at capped upper 999. The public fold-builder upper-only regression reached a missing refusal for upper869 at tip868; its upper868 refusal and upper999 accepting twin also execute construction, and the accepting body retains its omitted lower. Recorded preprod genesis/history supplies the accepting 120-second uncapped-window control. These are source-bound component checks, not a replacement for the required actual-node accepting leg. Earlier passing runs used the prior predicate and do not establish A022's upper869 refusal. The imported ledger/API limit remains explicit: Lean does not prove this horizon computation, usable-after-tip caller policy or zero-width correspondence; no Lean change is authorized.
